message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to pay the $50 jail fine or roll for doubles.

I have $304 and an orange monopoly with two houses each. I am mortgaged Indiana Avenue, Electric Company, and Water Works. The other players are in worse shape: p2 has no monopoly and p3 owns a pink monopoly with four houses each.

p3 also owns all four railroads and several other properties. p4 has only $40 cash and is heavily mortgaged. The pink monopoly with four houses each is extremely dangerous.

St. Charles and States each cost $625 with four houses. Virginia costs $700 with four houses. This is my second jail attempt after failing doubles on turn 101.

I can still roll for doubles or pay the $50 fine. If I fail again, I may be forced to pay on the third attempt. Staying in jail is safer because the pink monopoly sits right after it. Paying now and rolling risks landing on States or Virginia.

Rolling a 3 or 4 from jail lands on States or Virginia, both costing $625 and $700. A roll of 5 hits p3's Pennsylvania RR for $200. Only a 6 lands on St. James Place, my own property.

Rolling doubles from jail is risky. A 1-1 lands on Electric Company, which is safe because it is mortgaged. A 2-2 lands on Virginia Avenue with four houses for $700. The probability of landing on States or Virginia immediately is only about 14 percent combined.

Only a 2-2 doubles roll lands on Virginia Avenue for $700. The other five doubles rolls are safe, landing on St. James, Tennessee, Free Parking, or Chance. Paying the fine first is far riskier because it exposes me to the high-probability States and Virginia squares plus the $200 railroad rent. I have six orange houses to sell if I must pay.

Selling all six orange houses returns $300, giving me $604 total cash. That is still $21 short of the $625 rent on States Avenue and $96 short of the $700 rent on Virginia Avenue. I would need to mortgage properties as well.

Mortgaging an orange property to cover the $700 Virginia rent would cost $100 in interest and break the monopoly. Paying the $50 fine first leaves only $254, which is even worse. I will roll for doubles instead.

I still have one more turn to roll doubles before the fine becomes mandatory. While in jail, I continue collecting rent on my orange properties, which could help me if opponents land there. p4 is poor and on Virginia. p3 has $1071 and sits on Pennsylvania RR. p2 is on Marvin Gardens. I am checking who might reach my orange squares next.

p3 is positioned directly before my orange properties, so they could land on St. James or Tennessee and pay rent while I remain in jail. p4 has only $40 cash and could go bankrupt to me if she lands on my orange. I am verifying the exact two-house rent values for each orange property.

Two-house orange rent is $200 on St. James and Tennessee, and $220 on New York. p4 with $40 landing on St. James would need to mortgage Park Place or Boardwalk to survive. p3 can pay the rent easily. I will roll for doubles.
